L4: An inverter is one of the most important pieces of equipment in a solar energy system. It’s a device that converts direct current (DC) electricity, which is what a solar panel generates, to alternating current (AC) electricity, which the electrical grid uses. In DC, electricity is maintained at constant voltage in one direction. In AC, electricity flows in both directions in the circuit as the voltage changes from positive to negative.
L6: Fundamentally, an inverter accomplishes the DC-to-AC conversion by switching the direction of a DC input back and forth very rapidly. As a result, a DC input becomes an AC output. In addition, filters and other electronics can be used to produce a voltage that varies as a clean, repeating sine wave that can be injected into the power grid.

L161: 
L162: A DC-DC converter is equipment that converts DC into DC.
L163: Each IC or other component mounted on the board of the set has an intrinsic working voltage range, and in addition the required voltage accuracy differs from one component to another.

currentCard.prompt: Какой реактор поддерживает деление быстрыми нейтронами без обычного замедлителя?

answers.note: В водо-водяном реакторе вода первого контура под высоким давлением не кипит и нагревает отдельный парогенератор.
В кипящем реакторе вода закипает прямо в активной зоне, а пар идёт к турбине.
Тяжеловодный реактор использует оксид дейтерия как замедлитель и иногда как теплоноситель.
Быстрый реактор может превращать уран-238 в делящийся плутоний.

currentCard.explanation: Быстрый реактор поддерживает цепную реакцию на нейтронах высоких энергий без обычного замедлителя. Такой спектр позволяет эффективно превращать уран-238 в делящийся плутоний.

sixFieldLiteral.promptKey:
Какая система подаёт воду для отвода остаточного тепла от топлива после потери нормального охлаждения реактора?
Система аварийного охлаждения
sixFieldLiteral.explanation: Система аварийного охлаждения отводит тепло от активной зоны после потери нормального теплоносителя и ограничивает повреждение топлива. Её компоненты резервируют для сохранения функции при единичном отказе.
sixFieldLiteral.note0: Компоненты аварийного охлаждения резервируют, чтобы сохранить отвод тепла при единичном отказе.
sixFieldLiteral.note1: Аварийная защита быстро вводит отрицательную реактивность и прекращает цепную реакцию.
sixFieldLiteral.note2: Гермооболочка — прочное здание вокруг реактора, предназначенное удерживать радиоактивные вещества.
sixFieldLiteral.note3: Отрицательный температурный коэффициент означает падение реактивности при нагреве; вклад топлива и замедлителя оценивают отдельно.

currentFullCard.prompt: Какая система подаёт воду для отвода остаточного тепла от топлива после потери нормального охлаждения реактора?

answers.note: Компоненты аварийного охлаждения резервируют, чтобы сохранить отвод тепла при единичном отказе.
Аварийная защита быстро вводит отрицательную реактивность и прекращает цепную реакцию.
Гермооболочка — прочное здание вокруг реактора, предназначенное удерживать радиоактивные вещества.

physicalOriginalProof.title: How Pumped Storage Hydropower Works
physicalOriginalProof.passage: When power from the plant is needed, water flows from the upper reservoir through turbine(s) that rotate generator(s) to produce electricity. The water then flows into the lower reservoir where it remains until electricity demand lowers. When this occurs, the turbines spin backward to pump the water back into the upper reservoir so it can once again be used to generate electricity when needed.

physicalOriginalProof.title: How Pumped Storage Hydropower Works
physicalOriginalProof.passage: When power from the plant is needed, water flows from the upper reservoir through turbine(s) that rotate generator(s) to produce electricity. The water then flows into the lower reservoir where it remains until electricity demand lowers. When this occurs, the turbines spin backward to pump the water back into the upper reservoir so it can once again be used to generate electricity when needed.

physicalOriginalProof.sourceClass: original publisher primary page; institutional exposition
physicalOriginalProof.exactOriginalPassage: Electric utility companies use meters to measure how much electricity their customers use. fields.independentAssessment: EIA explicitly gives utilities kWh; kWh energy versus watts power,1000W=kW and1millionW=MW supported. Revised40W five-hour example teaches own energy unit, correcting unrelated meter-location fact.

proof.exactOriginalPassage:
Electric utilities and power plants generally measure electricity in kilowatthours (kWh). One kWh is one kilowatt generated for one hour. For example, if you use a 40-Watt (0.04 kW) light bulb for five hours, you have used 200 Wh, or 0.2 kWh, of electrical energy.
Utility companies measure and monitor electricity use with meters
Electric utility companies use meters to measure how much electricity their customers use. These meters are usually located on the outside of the building or home where the power line connects. In the past, electricity meters were mechanical devices that a utility employee had to read manually. Eventually, automated meters could periodically report electricity use to the utility. Today, many utilities use electronic smart meters. These meters wirelessly send power usage data in real time. Some advanced smart meters can even track the electricity use of individual devices and allow the utility or customer to control electricity use remotely.

physicalOriginalProof.title: Measuring Electricity — U.S. Energy Information Administration
physicalOriginalProof.sourceClass: original publisher primary page; institutional exposition
physicalOriginalProof.exactOriginalPassage: Electric utility companies use meters to measure how much electricity their customers use. These meters are usually located on the outside of the building or home where the power line connects. In the past, electricity meters were mechanical devices that a utility employee had to read manually. Eventually, automated meters could periodically report electricity use to the utility. Today, many utilities use electronic smart meters. These meters wirelessly send power usage data in real time. Some advanced smart meters can even track the electricity use of individual devices and allow the utility or customer to control electricity use remotely.

Most U.S. and world electricity generation is from electric power plants that use a turbine to drive electricity generators. In a turbine generator, a moving fluid—water, steam, combustion gases, or air—pushes a series of blades mounted on a rotor shaft. The force of the fluid on the blades spins (rotates) the rotor shaft of a generator. The generator, in turn, converts the mechanical (kinetic) energy of the rotor to electrical energy. Different types of turbines include steam turbines, combustion (gas) turbines, hydroelectric turbines, and wind turbines.
Steam turbines are used to generate most of the world’s electricity, and they accounted for about 42% of U.S. electricity generation in 2022. Most steam turbines have a boiler where fuel is burned to produce hot water and steam in a heat exchanger, and the steam powers a turbine that drives a generator. Nuclear power reactors use nuclear fuel rods to produce steam. Solar thermal power plants and most geothermal power plants use steam turbines. Most of the largest U.S. electric power plants use steam turbines.

Most electricity generation is from generators that are based on scientist Michael Faraday’s discovery in 1831. He found that moving a magnet inside a coil of wire makes (induces) an electric current flow through the wire. He made the first electricity generator, called a Faraday disk, which operates on the relationship between magnetism and electricity and led to the design of the electromagnetic generators we use today.
Electromagnetic generators use an electromagnet—a magnet produced by electricity—not a traditional magnet. A basic electromagnetic generator has a series of insulated wire coils that form a stationary cylinder—called a stator—surrounding an electromagnetic shaft—called a rotor. Turning the rotor makes an electric current flow in each section of the wire coil, and each section becomes a separate electric conductor. The currents in the individual sections combine to form one large current. This current is the electricity that moves from generators through power lines to consumers. Electromagnetic generators driven by kinetic (mechanical) prime movers account for nearly all U.S. electricity generation.
Turbine driven generators
Most U.S. and world electricity generation is from electric power plants that use a turbine to drive electricity generators. In a turbine generator, a moving fluid—water, steam, combustion gases, or air—pushes a series of blades mounted on a rotor shaft. The force of the fluid on the blades spins (rotates) the rotor shaft of a generator. The generator, in turn, converts the mechanical (kinetic) energy of the rotor to electrical energy. Different types of turbines include steam turbines, combustion (gas) turbines, hydroelectric turbines, and wind turbines.

physicalOriginalProof.sourceClass: original publisher primary page; institutional exposition
physicalOriginalProof.exactOriginalPassage: Biogas, which is also called renewable natural gas (RNG) or biomethane, is an energy-rich gas produced from biomass. Biogas is made up mostly of methane (CH4) (the main compound in fossil-based natural gas) and carbon dioxide (CO2). The composition of biogas varies from 45%–65% methane, depending on the material (feedstock) used to produce the biogas. Biogas is produced from biomass primarily through two processes: anaerobic decomposition and thermochemical conversion.

proof.exactOriginalPassage: The metric commonly used to classify an operating strategy is capacity factor. Capacity factor is the ratio of actual output to the total potential output over time. Because so many variables and considerations affect capacity factor, no strict definitions separate base load, intermediate, and peaking operating strategies. However, for general purposes, capacity factors of 70% or higher indicate base-load operation is occurring. Units that operate in peaking service tend to run at less than 15% capacity factor. Intermediate service falls between peaking and base load.

Коэффициент нагрузки — отношение средней нагрузки к пиковому значению за заданный период.
Это предельная мощность, которую станция может выдать в конкретных условиях.
Это количество электроэнергии, произведённое за некоторый период.

currentFullCard.explanation: Коэффициент использования мощности сопоставляет фактическую выработку станции с потенциальной за тот же период. Поэтому он отражает и простои, и переменность выпуска.

proof.exactOriginalPassage: The metric commonly used to classify an operating strategy is capacity factor. Capacity factor is the ratio of actual output to the total potential output over time. Because so many variables and considerations affect capacity factor, no strict definitions separate base load, intermediate, and peaking operating strategies. However, for general purposes, capacity factors of 70% or higher indicate base-load operation is occurring. Units that operate in peaking service tend to run at less than 15% capacity factor. Intermediate service falls between peaking and base load.

physicalOriginalProof.sourceClass: original publisher primary page/report; institutional exposition

physicalOriginalProof.sourceClass: original publisher primary page/report; institutional exposition
physicalOriginalProof.exactOriginalPassage: L7: A fuel cell uses the chemical energy of hydrogen or other fuels to efficiently produce electricity. L70@P4: Electrochemical capacitors, which are commercially called supercapacitors or ultracapacitors, are a
L71@P4: family of energy storage devices with remarkably high specific power compared with other
L72@P4: electrochemical storage devices. Supercapacitors do not require a solid dielectric layer between the
L73@P4: two electrodes, instead they store energy by accumulating electric charge on porous electrodes filled
L74@P4: with an electrolyte solution and separated by an insulating porous membrane. Supercapacitors offer
L75@P4: large specific capacitance and high power output. They can be charged and discharged very quickly,
L76@P4: offer excellent cycle life and long operational life, and operate over a broad temperature range. The
L77@P4: major drawbacks of supercapacitors are low energy density and a high self-discharge rate. For
L78@P4: example, a supercapacitor passively discharges from 100% to 50% in a month compared with only
L79@P4: 5% for a lithium-ion battery [1]. The high capital cost and low energy density of supercapacitors make
L80@P4: the unit cost of energy stored ($/kWh) more expensive than alternatives such as batteries. Their
L81@P4: attributes make them attractive for uses in which frequent small charges/discharges are required
L82@P4: (e.g., ensuring power quality or providing frequency regulation). Their attributes and cost make them
L83@P4: less attractive for long-duration energy storage, which favors technologies with low self-discharge
L84@P4: that cost less per unit of energy stored.

L151@P6: Types of Supercapacitors
L152@P6: Supercapacitors can be divided into three types based on the charge storing mechanism (Figure 2,
L153@P6: Table 1): electrochemical double-layer capacitors, pseudocapacitors, and hybrid electrochemical
L154@P6: capacitors.
L155@P6: Figure 2. Schematics of three types of supercapacitors: (a) electrochemical double-layer capacitor, (b)
L156@P6: pseudocapacitor, and (c) asymmetric/hybrid electrochemical capacitor. (Adapted from [10].)
L157@P6: Electrochemical double-layer capacitors (EDLCs) use two similar electrodes based on active
L158@P6: carbon to form two capacitors with the electrolyte (Figure 2(a)). Charges are distributed on the
L159@P6: surfaces by physical processes involving no chemical reactions. They exhibit a fast response to
L160@P6: charge/discharge and good cycling stability; however, they also exhibit a higher self-discharge rate.
L161@P6: The performance characteristics of an EDLC can be adjusted for different applications by changing
L162@P6: the electrolyte.
L163@P6: Pseudocapacitors (PCs) use transition metal oxide-based electrodes to form highly reversable
L164@P6: redox (faradaic) reactions, which store energy by transferring charge between the electrode and the
L165@P6: electrolyte (Figure 2(b)). These faradaic processes allow PCs to achieve greater capacitances and
L166@P6: energy densities than EDLCs, which involve only the electric double-layer effect at the
L167@P6: electrode/electrolyte interface and no reactions at the electrodes.
L151@P5: Volt-Ampere Reactive to Support Grid Reliability
L152@P5: Introduction
L153@P5: The first electrical grids in the United States were small, typically consisting of a local source of generation (often
L154@P5: hydro) and the wiring necessary to light a town on demand—and also supply any industrial motor load made
L155@P5: possible by the grid’s proximity. The generator supplied any voltage support required as well as the real power
L156@P5: that made life suddenly so much easier for those with access to these initial grids.
L157@P5: As these isolated power grids expanded—sometimes to reach new, more distant concentrations of residential or
L158@P5: industrial load and later, to intertie with other grids for efficiency and reliability improvements—voltage support
L159@P5: was sometimes necessary close to load concentrations that were too distant for the generator(s) to meet the
L160@P5: need. A synchronous condenser was often installed in this circumstance. A synchronous condenser is a motor
L161@P5: that is designed in some ways similarly to a generator, so that it can raise or lower system voltage around it.
L162@P5: However, since it lacks a prime mover to turn it (e.g., a waterwheel or coal-fueled, steam-driven turbine), it
L163@P5: consumes electricity while regulating voltage rather than generating it. Capacitors, currently the most frequently
L164@P5: used electrical device to provide system voltage support distant from generation, were at this early time quite
L165@P5: unreliable, and were not available in sizes to supply significant voltage support.
L166@P5: Voltage support from generators and synchronous condensers flows instantaneously to the power system when
L167@P5: needed—a result of the inertial properties of rotating machines, and the laws of physics that govern electricity—

sourceChecks.originalPassage:
L79@P4: Compressed air energy storage (CAES) is one of the many energy storage options that can store
L80@P4: electric energy in the form of potential energy (compressed air) and can be deployed near central
L81@P4: power plants or distribution centers. In response to demand, the stored energy can be discharged
L82@P4: by expanding the stored air with a turboexpander generator. An attractive feature of this technology
L83@P4: is the relative simplicity of the process—a compressor is powered by available electricity to compress
L84@P4: air (charging), which is then stored in a chamber until the energy is needed. During discharge, the
L85@P4: compressed air is run through a turboexpander to generate electricity back to the grid.
L86@P4: The attributes of CAES that make it an attractive option include a wide range of energy storage
L87@P4: capacity (from a few megawatts to several gigawatts), an environmentally friendly process
L88@P4: (especially when no fossil fuel is used for combustion), long life and durability, low self-discharge
L89@P4: (due to a loss of pressure and temperature), and the low cost of the energy stored. Some of the
L90@P4: challenges of this technology include high upfront capital costs, the need for heat during the
L91@P4: expansion step, lower round-trip efficiency (RTE), siting and permitting challenges, difficulty in
L92@P4: identifying and preparing natural caverns for storage, low depth of discharge, and longer response
sourceChecks.readerReason: Compression storage chamber/underground cavern, turboexpander actual DOE body.

L2565@P90: Gravity Energy Storage
L2566@P90: Gravity-based ESSs can take many forms, from pressurized water that lifts a piston within a mined shaft
L2567@P90: to heavy bricks that are lifted by a crane to store energy. In each case, the stored energy is converted
L2568@P90: into kinetic energy that generates electricity using generators. The systems offer the potential for
L2569@P90: scalable energy outputs, for example doubling shaft depth increases stored energy content by a factor
L2570@P90: of four; whereas, for storage based on lifting heavy blocks, scaling with respect to energy is enabled by
L2571@P90: increasing the mass of each block. The different types of gravity ESSs covered in this section are:
L2572@P90: ▪ Heavy bricks lifted by cranes
L2573@P90: ▪ Rail-based gravity storage
L2574@P90: ▪ Pressurized water that lifts a heavy piston within a mined shaft with power equipment below
L2575@P90: ground
L2576@P90: ▪ Pressurized water that lifts a heavy piston within a mined shaft with power equipment above
L2577@P90: ground.
L2578@P90: Gravity-based systems use stored gravitational potential energy for conversion to electricity via a
L2579@P90: generator. Energy is stored by lifting 35-ton concrete blocks using a six-arm crane powered by a motor
L2580@P90: during periods of excess electricity and electricity is generated by dropping the blocks with the motor
L2581@P90-91: running in reverse (John, 2019; Pedretti, 2021; Spector, 2018; Vault, 2021). The control software directs Energy Storage Grand Challenge Cost and Performance Assessment 2022 August 2022

L151@P5: Volt-Ampere Reactive to Support Grid Reliability
L152@P5: Introduction
L153@P5: The first electrical grids in the United States were small, typically consisting of a local source of generation (often
L154@P5: hydro) and the wiring necessary to light a town on demand—and also supply any industrial motor load made
L155@P5: possible by the grid’s proximity. The generator supplied any voltage support required as well as the real power
L156@P5: that made life suddenly so much easier for those with access to these initial grids.
L157@P5: As these isolated power grids expanded—sometimes to reach new, more distant concentrations of residential or
L158@P5: industrial load and later, to intertie with other grids for efficiency and reliability improvements—voltage support
L159@P5: was sometimes necessary close to load concentrations that were too distant for the generator(s) to meet the
L160@P5: need. A synchronous condenser was often installed in this circumstance. A synchronous condenser is a motor
L161@P5: that is designed in some ways similarly to a generator, so that it can raise or lower system voltage around it.
L162@P5: However, since it lacks a prime mover to turn it (e.g., a waterwheel or coal-fueled, steam-driven turbine), it
L163@P5: consumes electricity while regulating voltage rather than generating it. Capacitors, currently the most frequently
L164@P5: used electrical device to provide system voltage support distant from generation, were at this early time quite
L165@P5: unreliable, and were not available in sizes to supply significant voltage support.
L166@P5: Voltage support from generators and synchronous condensers flows instantaneously to the power system when
L167@P5: needed—a result of the inertial properties of rotating machines, and the laws of physics that govern electricity—

L79@P4: Compressed air energy storage (CAES) is one of the many energy storage options that can store
L80@P4: electric energy in the form of potential energy (compressed air) and can be deployed near central
L81@P4: power plants or distribution centers. In response to demand, the stored energy can be discharged
L82@P4: by expanding the stored air with a turboexpander generator. An attractive feature of this technology
L83@P4: is the relative simplicity of the process—a compressor is powered by available electricity to compress
L84@P4: air (charging), which is then stored in a chamber until the energy is needed. During discharge, the
L85@P4: compressed air is run through a turboexpander to generate electricity back to the grid.
L86@P4: The attributes of CAES that make it an attractive option include a wide range of energy storage
L87@P4: capacity (from a few megawatts to several gigawatts), an environmentally friendly process
L88@P4: (especially when no fossil fuel is used for combustion), long life and durability, low self-discharge
L89@P4: (due to a loss of pressure and temperature), and the low cost of the energy stored. Some of the
L90@P4: challenges of this technology include high upfront capital costs, the need for heat during the
L91@P4: expansion step, lower round-trip efficiency (RTE), siting and permitting challenges, difficulty in
L92@P4: identifying and preparing natural caverns for storage, low depth of discharge, and longer response

physicalOriginalProof.title: How Electricity Is Generated — U.S. EIA
physicalOriginalProof.sourceClass: original publisher primary page/report; institutional exposition
physicalOriginalProof.exactOriginalPassage: Steam and combustion turbines can be operated as stand-alone generators in a single cycle or combined in a sequential, combined cycle. Combined-cycle systems use combustion gases from one turbine to generate more electricity in another turbine. Most combined-cycle systems have separate generators for each turbine. In single-shaft combined-cycle systems, both turbines may drive a single generator. In 2022, combined-cycle power plants supplied about 34% of U.S. net electricity generation.

Correct note adds exhaust-to-steam fact beyond asked generator arrangement.

L53: ### Binary-Cycle Power Plant
L54: Binary-cycle geothermal power plants can use lower temperature geothermal resources, making them an important technology for deploying geothermal electricity production in more locations. Binary-cycle geothermal power plants differ from dry steam and flash steam systems in that the geothermal reservoir fluids never come into contact with the power plant’s turbine units. Low-temperature (below 182°C/360°F) geothermal fluids pass through a heat exchanger with a secondary, or "binary," fluid.
L55: This binary fluid has a much lower boiling point than water, and the modest heat from the geothermal fluid causes it to flash to vapor, which then drives the turbines, spins the generators, and creates electricity.

L6: All turbine engines have the cite15†core components of a cite16†compressor , cite17†combustion section , and cite18†power turbine which drives the compressor. The cite19†thermodynamics of all turbine engines are similar. To understand how a propulsion system works, we must study the basic thermodynamics of cite20†gases . Gases have various cite21†properties that we can observe with our senses, including the gas cite22†pressure p, cite23†temperature T, mass, and cite24†volume V that contains the gas.
L7: Careful, scientific observation has determined that these cite25†variables are related to one another, and the values of these properties determine the cite26†state of the gas. A thermodynamic process, such as heating or cite27†compressing the gas, changes the values of the state variables in a manner which is described by the cite28†laws of thermodynamics .
L8: The cite29†work done by a gas and the cite30†heat transferred to a gas depend on the beginning and ending states of the gas and on the process used to change the state. It is possible to perform a series of processes, in which the state is changed during each process, but the gas eventually returns to its original state. Such a series of processes is called a cite31†cycle and forms the basis for understanding engine operation.
L9: On this page we discuss the Brayton Thermodynamic Cycle which is used in all gas turbine engines. The figure shows a cite32†T-s diagram of the Brayton cycle. Using the turbine engine cite33†station numbering system , we begin with cite34†free stream conditions at station 0. In cruising flight, the cite35†inlet slows the air stream as it is brought to the cite16†compressor face at station 2.
L10: As the flow slows, some of the energy associated with the aircraft velocity cite36†increases the static cite22†pressure of the air and the flow is compressed. Ideally, the compression is cite27†isentropic and the static cite23†temperature is also increased as shown on the plot. The compressor does cite37†work on the gas and increases the pressure and temperature isentropically to station 3 the compressor exit. Since the compression is ideally isentropic, a vertical line on the T-s diagram describes the process.
L11: In reality, the compression is not isentropic and the compression process line leans to the right because of the increase in cite38†entropy of the flow. The cite39†combustion process in the cite17†burner occurs at constant pressure from station 3 to station 4. The temperature increase depends on the type of fuel used and the cite40†fuel-air ratio . The hot exhaust is then passed through the cite18†power turbine in which cite41†work is done by the flow from station 4 to station 5.

L6: All turbine engines have the cite15†core components of a cite16†compressor , cite17†combustion section , and cite18†power turbine which drives the compressor. The cite19†thermodynamics of all turbine engines are similar. To understand how a propulsion system works, we must study the basic thermodynamics of cite20†gases . Gases have various cite21†properties that we can observe with our senses, including the gas cite22†pressure p, cite23†temperature T, mass, and cite24†volume V that contains the gas.
L7: Careful, scientific observation has determined that these cite25†variables are related to one another, and the values of these properties determine the cite26†state of the gas. A thermodynamic process, such as heating or cite27†compressing the gas, changes the values of the state variables in a manner which is described by the cite28†laws of thermodynamics .
L8: The cite29†work done by a gas and the cite30†heat transferred to a gas depend on the beginning and ending states of the gas and on the process used to change the state. It is possible to perform a series of processes, in which the state is changed during each process, but the gas eventually returns to its original state. Such a series of processes is called a cite31†cycle and forms the basis for understanding engine operation.
L9: On this page we discuss the Brayton Thermodynamic Cycle which is used in all gas turbine engines. The figure shows a cite32†T-s diagram of the Brayton cycle. Using the turbine engine cite33†station numbering system , we begin with cite34†free stream conditions at station 0. In cruising flight, the cite35†inlet slows the air stream as it is brought to the cite16†compressor face at station 2.
L10: As the flow slows, some of the energy associated with the aircraft velocity cite36†increases the static cite22†pressure of the air and the flow is compressed. Ideally, the compression is cite27†isentropic and the static cite23†temperature is also increased as shown on the plot. The compressor does cite37†work on the gas and increases the pressure and temperature isentropically to station 3 the compressor exit. Since the compression is ideally isentropic, a vertical line on the T-s diagram describes the process.
L11: In reality, the compression is not isentropic and the compression process line leans to the right because of the increase in cite38†entropy of the flow. The cite39†combustion process in the cite17†burner occurs at constant pressure from station 3 to station 4. The temperature increase depends on the type of fuel used and the cite40†fuel-air ratio . The hot exhaust is then passed through the cite18†power turbine in which cite41†work is done by the flow from station 4 to station 5.

sourceScopesRead.originalPassage:
Nepal
red with a blue border around the unique shape of two overlapping right triangles; the smaller, upper triangle bears a white stylized moon and the larger, lower triangle displays a white 12-pointed sun; the color red represents the rhododendron (Nepal's national flower) and is a sign of victory and bravery, the blue border signifies peace and harmony; the two right triangles are a combination of two single pennons (pennants) that originally symbolized the Himalaya Mountains while their charges represented the families of the king (upper) and the prime minister, but today they are understood to denote Hinduism and Buddhism, the country's two main religions; the moon represents the serenity of the Nepalese people and the shade and cool weather in the Himalayas, while the sun depicts the heat and higher temperatures of the lower parts of Nepal; the moon and the sun are also said to express the hope that the nation will endure as long as these heavenly bodies
note: Nepal is the only country in the world whose flag is not rectangular or square

sourceProofs.exactOriginalPassage:
Belize
blue with a narrow red stripe along the top and the bottom edges; centered is a large white disk bearing the coat of arms; the coat of arms features a shield flanked by two workers in front of a mahogany tree with the related motto SUB UMBRA FLOREO (I Flourish in the Shade) on a scroll at the bottom, all encircled by a green garland of 50 mahogany leaves; the colors are those of the two main political parties: blue for the PUP and red for the UDP; various elements of the coat of arms - the figures, the tools, the mahogany tree, and the garland of leaves - recall the logging industry that led to British settlement of Belize
note: Belize's flag is the only national flag that depicts human beings; two British overseas territories, Montserrat and the British Virgin Islands, also depict humans

wholeCardRead.prompt: Кто написал музыку мюзикла «Призрак Оперы»?

answers.note: Лин-Мануэль Миранда написал музыку, либретто и тексты песен «Гамильтона». Партитура сочетает хип-хоп, джаз, R&B и бродвейские традиции.
Эндрю Ллойд Уэббер также сочинил «Кошек» и «Эвиту». Премьера «Призрака Оперы» прошла в Лондоне.
Клод-Мишель Шёнберг создал «Отверженных» вместе с Аленом Бублилем. Мюзикл основан на романе Виктора Гюго.
Леонард Бернстайн написал партитуру «Вестсайдской истории». Сюжет переносит конфликт Ромео и Джульетты в Нью-Йорк.

wholeCardRead.explanation: Музыку «Призрака Оперы» написал Эндрю Ллойд Уэббер. Он также сочинил «Кошек» и «Эвиту», а премьера «Призрака Оперы» прошла в Лондоне.

source.title: Andrew Lloyd Webber Musicals — The Phantom of the Opera

Лин-Мануэль Миранда написал музыку, либретто и тексты песен «Гамильтона». Партитура сочетает хип-хоп, джаз, R&B и бродвейские традиции.
Клод-Мишель Шёнберг создал «Отверженных» вместе с Аленом Бублилем. Мюзикл основан на романе Виктора Гюго.
Эндрю Ллойд Уэббер также сочинил «Кошек» и «Эвиту». Премьера «Призрака Оперы» прошла в Лондоне.

currentFullCard.explanation: Музыку «Отверженных» написал Клод-Мишель Шёнберг. Он работал над мюзиклом с Аленом Бублилем; основой стал роман Виктора Гюго.

source.title: Les Misérables official tour — Cast & Creative

note2.literal: Тенор — высокий мужской голос. В романтической опере ему часто поручают роль героя.

note3.literal: Сопрано — самый высокий женский голос; так поют Виолетту в «Травиате» и Царицу ночи в «Волшебной флейте».

Гофмансталь написал для Штрауса либретто «Электры» по Софоклу; оперу представили в 1909 году.
Гилберт и Салливан работали вместе более 25 лет и создали четырнадцать опер.
Бойто переработал либретто «Симона Бокканегры». Новую версию успешно поставили в Ла Скала в 1881 году.

Какая форма требует после средней части вернуться к началу и украсить повтор?
Ария da capo

explanation.literal: Ария da capo строится как A–B–A: после контрастной середины певец возвращается к началу и может украсить мелодию. Такой тип арии встречается в «Джустино» Генделя.

note0.literal: В «Джустино» Генделя звучат арии da capo; итальянское выражение означает «с начала».

note1.literal: На премьере «Джустино» в 1737 году заглавную партию пел кастрат Доменико Аннибали.

note2.literal: Бассо континуо сочетает басовую линию, клавишный и низкий мелодический инструмент.

note3.literal: «Джустино» Генделя относится к opera seria: в истории действуют император и богиня Фортуна.

promptKey.literal:
Как называется итальянская традиция красивого гибкого пения, связанная с Россини и Беллини?
Бельканто

explanation.literal: Бельканто — итальянская традиция «красивого пения», связанная с Россини и Беллини. Она подчёркивает чистоту тембра, выразительную фразировку и вокальные украшения.

note0.literal: «Сельская честь» Масканьи дала толчок веризму: на сцене действуют обычные люди, а конфликт приводит к насилию.

note1.literal: Бельканто ценит чистоту тона, выразительную фразировку и украшения мелодии.

note2.literal: «Волшебная флейта» — зингшпиль; Моцарт написал в этом жанре и «Похищение из сераля».

note3.literal: Оффенбах сделал оперетту международным жанром благодаря, среди прочего, «Орфею в аду».

Для какого типа голоса написана заглавная партия «Кармен»?

explanation.literal: Заглавную партию «Кармен» обычно исполняет меццо-сопрано. Кармен поёт знаменитую хабанеру в первом акте оперы Бизе.

note0.literal: Драматический тенор должен прорезать голосом большой оркестр; пример — партия Отелло у Верди.

note1.literal: Партия Зарастро относится к басу-профундо с особенно низким и тёмным тембром.

note2.literal: Кармен поёт хабанеру в первом акте; в ней любовь сравнивается с непокорной птицей.

note3.literal: Моцарт написал партию Царицы ночи для Йозефы Хофер, которая исполняла её десять лет.

sourceProofs.exactOriginalBodyPassage: The Beggar’s Opera – John Gay John Gay’s The Beggar’s Opera , is one of the most famous examples of a Ballad Opera. This new genre was a big hit with audiences in the 18th Century, as it satirised Italian Opera –which was hugely popular at the time. Instead of grand productions and elaborate scores, a Ballad Opera told stories of everyday people using songs audiences would already know, instead of composing original music. For example, The Beggar’s Opera featured music from the famous composer, Handel. It follows the story of characters who would have been on the streets of London at that time, including a group of thieves and ladies of the night. However, it was a form of political satire that took jabs at the ‘higher classes’ including the government and those in high society. Although tackling difficult themes of poverty and political corruption, it’s a comic opera that is still popular with audiences today. Close dialog Video Anna Bolena – Gaetano Donizetti Anna

sourceProofs.exactOriginalBodyPassage: The Beggar’s Opera – John Gay John Gay’s The Beggar’s Opera , is one of the most famous examples of a Ballad Opera. This new genre was a big hit with audiences in the 18th Century, as it satirised Italian Opera –which was hugely popular at the time. Instead of grand productions and elaborate scores, a Ballad Opera told stories of everyday people using songs audiences would already know, instead of composing original music. For example, The Beggar’s Opera featured music from the famous composer, Handel. It follows the story of characters who would have been on the streets of London at that time, including a group of thieves and ladies of the night. However, it was a form of political satire that took jabs at the ‘higher classes’ including the government and those in high society. Although tackling difficult themes of poverty and political corruption, it’s a comic opera that is still popular with audiences today. Close dialog Video Anna Bolena – Gaetano Donizetti Anna

wholeCardRead.prompt: В Байройтском театре оркестр скрывали от публики, чтобы музыканты не отвлекали её от спектакля. Где по этой схеме должен играть оркестр?

answers.note: Суфлёр может давать певцу подсказку жестом.
Просцениум расположен между занавесом и оркестровой ямой.

sourceProofs.title: CATS Official — The Origins of CATS
sourceProofs.sourceClass: original theatrical rights-holder or production company history
sourceProofs.exactOriginalBodyPassage: Eliot’s Old Possum’s Book of Practical Cats is a collection of playful poems he wrote for his grandchildren. Originally in letter form, the verses went down such a treat that Eliot decided to publish them in 1939 so that children everywhere could delight in them, too. One such child was a 6-year-old Andrew Lloyd Webber, whose mother read the poems to him at bedtime and who, as he grew up, revisited the poems himself time and time again. (1925) Almost 25 years later, a now grown-up Andrew wondered whether he could set his beloved childhood poems to music. Up until this point Andrew’s process had to been to first write the music before handing over to a lyricist for the words. Andrew presented four newly composed settings from T.S. Eliot’s collection at his 4th Sydmonton Festival which received a wholly positive round of applause, encouraging him to further develop the piece.

sourceProofs.exactOriginalBodyPassage: Eliot’s Old Possum’s Book of Practical Cats is a collection of playful poems he wrote for his grandchildren. Originally in letter form, the verses went down such a treat that Eliot decided to publish them in 1939 so that children everywhere could delight in them, too. One such child was a 6-year-old Andrew Lloyd Webber, whose mother read the poems to him at bedtime and who, as he grew up, revisited the poems himself time and time again. (1925) Almost 25 years later, a now grown-up Andrew wondered whether he could set his beloved childhood poems to music. Up until this point Andrew’s process had to been to first write the music before handing over to a lyricist for the words. Andrew presented four newly composed settings from T.S. Eliot’s collection at his 4th Sydmonton Festival which received a wholly positive round of applause, encouraging him to further develop the piece.

sourceProofs.title: CATS Official — The Origins of CATS
sourceProofs.sourceClass: original theatrical rights-holder or production company history
sourceProofs.exactOriginalBodyPassage: Eliot’s Old Possum’s Book of Practical Cats is a collection of playful poems he wrote for his grandchildren. Originally in letter form, the verses went down such a treat that Eliot decided to publish them in 1939 so that children everywhere could delight in them, too. One such child was a 6-year-old Andrew Lloyd Webber, whose mother read the poems to him at bedtime and who, as he grew up, revisited the poems himself time and time again. (1925) Almost 25 years later, a now grown-up Andrew wondered whether he could set his beloved childhood poems to music. Up until this point Andrew’s process had to been to first write the music before handing over to a lyricist for the words. Andrew presented four newly composed settings from T.S. Eliot’s collection at his 4th Sydmonton Festival which received a wholly positive round of applause, encouraging him to further develop the piece.

sourceProofs.exactOriginalBodyPassage: The Beggar’s Opera – John Gay John Gay’s The Beggar’s Opera , is one of the most famous examples of a Ballad Opera. This new genre was a big hit with audiences in the 18th Century, as it satirised Italian Opera –which was hugely popular at the time. Instead of grand productions and elaborate scores, a Ballad Opera told stories of everyday people using songs audiences would already know, instead of composing original music. For example, The Beggar’s Opera featured music from the famous composer, Handel. It follows the story of characters who would have been on the streets of London at that time, including a group of thieves and ladies of the night. However, it was a form of political satire that took jabs at the ‘higher classes’ including the government and those in high society. Although tackling difficult themes of poverty and political corruption, it’s a comic opera that is still popular with audiences today. Close dialog Video Anna Bolena – Gaetano Donizetti Anna

It’s name was derived from a theatre of the same name in Paris. However, unlike other forms of comic opera, works did not necessarily have to be humorous to be classed as ‘opera comique’. Instead, they could be dramas or even serious operas as long as they featured spoken dialogue and arias.
